name: Introductory Earth Sciences
description: Introduction to the materials of the Earth and the geological processes that shape the planet across deep time; rocks, minerals, plate tectonics, surface processes, and Earth history.
prerequisites: None stated; corequisite for lab is EARTH 121L.

name: Introductory Earth Sciences Laboratory
description: Hands‑on laboratory accompanying EARTH 121 covering mineral/rock identification, topographic maps, and basic geologic problem‑solving.

name: Introductory Environmental Sciences
description: Foundational concepts in environmental science including biogeochemical cycles, water, air, soils, energy and climate, with emphasis on human impacts and sustainability.
prerequisites: None stated; corequisite for lab is EARTH 122L.

name: Introductory Environmental Sciences Laboratory
description: Laboratory exercises supporting EARTH 122 focusing on environmental sampling and analysis.

name: Structural Geology and Tectonics (introductory)
description: Introduction to structures present in the Earth’s crust (folds, faults, fabric) and the stress/strain responsible for their development; basics of brittle/ductile deformation and plate‑tectonic context.

name: Mineralogy
description: Composition, structure and physical properties of rock‑forming minerals; techniques for mineral identification (hand specimen and microscopy).

name: Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology
description: Description, classification and origin of igneous and metamorphic rocks; phase equilibria and tectonic settings.

name: Introduction to Geochemistry
description: Fundamentals of geochemistry including thermodynamics of geochemical systems, kinetics, isotopes, and aqueous chemistry; applications to natural waters and environmental problems.
prerequisites: Prereq: CHE 102 or 120, and MATH 118/119/128/138/148 (or equivalent).

name: Sedimentology and Stratigraphy
description: Principles of sediment transport and deposition; facies analysis; stratigraphic correlation; interpretation of ancient environments.

name: Applied Geophysics
description: Overview of geophysical methods for subsurface investigation (seismic, gravity, magnetic, electrical, ground‑penetrating radar) with case studies in resource and engineering settings.
prerequisites: Prereq: Math/physics background at 2nd year level.

name: Structural Geology of the Earth’s Crust
description: Stress and strain in the Earth’s crust; rheology of rocks; analysis of folds, faults, shear zones and fabrics; evolution of mountain belts; introduction to plate kinematics.

name: Engineering Geology
description: Application of geology to engineering: rock and soil properties, mass movements, landslides, hazards; site investigation, sampling, logging and in‑situ testing for foundations and slopes.

name: Basin Analysis
description: Processes controlling the formation and evolution of sedimentary basins; subsidence mechanisms, sediment routing, and tectono‑stratigraphic interpretation of basin fills.

name: Water‑Rock Interaction
description: Thermodynamics and kinetics of mineral–fluid reactions; aqueous geochemistry; modeling of water–rock systems relevant to environmental and hydrogeological problems.

name: Energy from the Earth
description: Earth’s energy resources and the grid: geothermal, hydrocarbons, and emerging subsurface energy technologies; evaluation of reservoirs and environmental implications.

name: Geotechnical Site Investigation
description: Methods for site investigation in soil and rock: boreholes, sampling, logging, in‑situ tests; lab testing; interpretation and reporting for geotechnical design.

name: Mineral Resources
description: Nature, origin, discovery and evaluation of mineral deposits; ore‑forming processes and exploration methods; environmental and social considerations in mining.

name: Geomicrobiology
description: Interactions between microbes and geologic processes; biogeochemical cycling of elements and applications to remediation and resource formation.

name: Organismal and Evolutionary Ecology
description: Introduction to ecology and evolution at the organismal level: scientific reasoning, population genetics, life histories, population and community ecology, macroevolution, systematics.
prerequisites: Often paired with BIOL 150 lab; Antireq sometimes BIOL 251 (see calendar).

name: Introduction to Microbiology
description: Structure, metabolism, genetics and ecology of microorganisms with emphasis on bacteria; laboratory introduces sterile technique and microbial analysis.
prerequisites: Prereq: BIOL 130/130L or equivalent first‑year biology.

name: Introduction to Applied Microbiology
description: Applied aspects of microbiology in health, environment and industry; control of microorganisms; beneficial uses in biotechnology.

name: Animal Physiology 1
description: Cellular and systems physiology in animals with emphasis on homeostasis, neurophysiology, muscle, and endocrine function.
prerequisites: Prereq: BIOL 130/273 co‑requisites vary by term (see calendar).

name: Principles of Human Physiology 1
description: Physiology of major organ systems at the cellular and systems levels; neural, muscular, cardiovascular, respiratory, renal and endocrine physiology with applications.

name: Biostatistics
description: Statistical reasoning and analysis for biological data: experimental design, probability, estimation, hypothesis testing and regression using real datasets.

name: Evolution
description: Evidence and mechanisms of evolution including natural selection, genetic drift, mutation, gene flow, speciation and macroevolutionary patterns.
prerequisites: Prereq: 2nd‑year BIOL and stats background (see calendar).

name: Microbiology of Environmental Systems
description: Microbial communities and processes in soil, water and engineered environments; biogeochemical cycles; methods for environmental microbiology.

name: Molecular Genetics
description: Gene structure and function in prokaryotes and eukaryotes; DNA replication, transcription, translation; gene regulation; recombinant DNA techniques.
prerequisites: Prereq: BIOL 238/239 level genetics; see calendar.

name: Eukaryotic Microbiology
description: Biology of fungi and protists; diversity, physiology and roles in ecosystems and disease; lab emphasizes isolation and identification.

name: Stream and River Ecology
description: Ecology of running waters; physical and biological processes in streams and rivers; field and analytical methods.
prerequisites: Prereq: BIOL 150 or ENVS 200 level ecology background.

name: Tropical Ecosystems
description: Fundamental concepts of terrestrial ecosystems in tropical climates: biophysical context, resource systems and conservation issues; case‑study based.
prerequisites: Prereq: One of ENVS 200, BIOL 150, or BIOL 251.

name: Plant Physiology
description: Physiology of plants including photosynthesis, water relations, mineral nutrition, growth regulators and stress physiology.

name: Human Molecular Genetics
description: Genetics of human disease; mapping and identifying disease genes; genomics, functional assays and ethical considerations.

name: Evolutionary Ecology
description: Evolutionary processes applied to ecological interactions and life‑history strategies; natural selection in populations, adaptation, and constraints.

name: Regional Human Anatomy
description: Regional anatomy of the limbs and trunk, with brief introduction to CNS and cardiovascular systems; focus on bones, muscles and neurovasculature.

name: Biomechanics of Human Movement
description: Mechanical basis of human movement; functional anatomy, muscle and passive tissue mechanics, anthropometry, EMG, linked segment mechanics; applications to clinical, occupational and athletic contexts.

name: Biomechanics of Human Movement Laboratory
description: Laboratory supporting KIN 121 with practical tools for biomechanical assessment of human movement.

name: Advanced Biomechanics of Human Movement
description: Measurement, analytical and computation techniques for multi‑segment, dynamic analysis of human activity; applications across occupational, clinical and sport settings.

name: Advanced Biomechanics of Human Movement Laboratory
description: Laboratory providing advanced practical tools aligned with KIN 221 content.

name: Fundamentals of Neuroscience
description: Foundations in the nervous system control of movement, cognition and learning.
prerequisites: Coreq for majors: KIN 255L. Prereq: BIOL 273, PSYCH 101, KIN 104L.

name: Fundamentals of Neuroscience Laboratory
description: Practical tools to assess nervous system control of movement, cognition and learning; complements KIN 255 lectures.

name: Introduction to Neurological Disorders
description: Overview of selected neurological disorders and implications for physical activity across neuromuscular, perceptual‑motor, and cardiorespiratory domains.

name: Task Analysis
description: Methods to identify, describe and analyze how people interact with their environment and with each other; HFE applications; didactic, case‑study and experiential learning.

name: Musculoskeletal Injuries in Sport and Activity
description: Mechanisms of injury, tissue biomechanics, pathophysiology, assessment, management, and prevention of sport/activity injuries.
prerequisites: Prereq: (KIN 100 & 100L) or (BIOL 201/301); Level at least 3A Faculty of Health.

name: Sensory Systems Neuroscience
description: Neural bases of sensory systems with applications to movement and perception; may cover vision, audition, proprioception, vestibular function.

name: Neuromuscular Integration
description: Clinical neurophysiological concepts for control of human movement; bioelectrical origins and applications to diagnosis following nervous system injury.
prerequisites: Prereq: BIOL 273 or PSYCH 261; Level at least 3A.

name: Aging, Health and Physical Activity
description: Physical, mental, and social changes with aging and implications of physical activity; barriers and strategies to improve participation at different scales.

name: Human Posture, Balance and Gait
description: Kinematics, kinetics, and neural control of standing, stepping, walking and running; measurement techniques; applications to aging and pathology.

name: Biomechanical Modelling
description: Quantitative measurement and analysis of the musculoskeletal system; multi‑segment dynamics; EMG in movement control; applications to normal, athletic and pathological movement.

name: Nonlinear Optimization
description: First course in the mathematics of nonlinear optimization: optimality conditions for unconstrained and constrained problems, convexity and applications, computational techniques and their analysis.
prerequisites: Prereq: One of CO 250/350/352/255/355; and MATH 128 (min 70%) or MATH 138 or 148.

name: Introduction to Game Theory
description: Mathematical analysis of games and strategic behaviour; normal and extensive form games, Nash equilibria, mixed strategies, repeated and evolutionary games; applications.

name: Combinatorial Optimization
description: Topics in combinatorial optimization such as matching, matroids, network flows, cuts and polyhedral methods; algorithms and proofs of optimality.

name: Continuous Optimization
description: Continuous optimization theory and algorithms with applications; gradient methods, Newton and quasi‑Newton, constrained optimization.

name: Algorithmic Game Theory
description: Algorithmic and computational aspects of game theory including auctions, pricing, matchings and equilibria; incentive compatibility and mechanism design basics.
prerequisites: Prereq: CO 456 or CS/CO background; see calendar.

name: Introduction to Entrepreneurship
description: Key concepts in entrepreneurship, opportunity recognition, customer discovery, value propositions, business models and communicating venture ideas.

name: Entrepreneurship Principles and Practice
description: Applies entrepreneurial tools to develop, test and iterate venture concepts; customer interviews, MVPs, experiments and pitches.
prerequisites: Prereq: Level at least 2A or consent.

name: Foundations of Venture Planning
description: Business planning fundamentals for new ventures including market sizing, go‑to‑market, operations and finance; prepares for capstone planning courses.
prerequisites: Prereq: BET 100 or experience (varies by term).

name: Applied Social Entrepreneurship
description: Students design and execute impact‑focused ventures addressing social or environmental challenges; emphasizes implementation and measurement of impact.

name: Interdisciplinary Design Project 1
description: First course in a two‑course interdisciplinary engineering design sequence. Teams formulate a problem/opportunity, develop a feasible proposal and plan, generate/evaluate solutions, and manage risks; deliver a report/presentation.
prerequisites: Prereq: Level at least 4A Engineering; Instructor consent required.

name: Interdisciplinary Design Project 2
description: Continuation of GENE 403 focusing on implementation and verification (analysis, test or prototype), and communication of the design solution; continued attention to safety, regulatory, sustainability and ethics.
prerequisites: Prereq: GENE 403; Level at least 4A Engineering; Instructor consent required.

name: Sustainability for Engineers
description: Engineering approaches to sustainability across environmental, social and economic domains; tools for assessment and design for sustainability.

name: Tropical Ecosystems
description: Biophysical aspects of tropical ecosystems, resource systems (forest and agro‑ecosystems) and current conservation issues; case‑study based. Often includes a field component.
prerequisites: Prereq: One of ENVS 200, BIOL 150, BIOL 251; instructor consent often required for field offering.

name: Transit Planning and Operations
description: Historical evolution of transit; vehicle dynamics and travel time; scheduling; system operations and measures of effectiveness; transit network planning objectives and service design.
prerequisites: Prereq: As listed in offering; often cross‑listed with CIVE 440/641 and PLAN 678.

name: Global Environmental Governance
description: International organizations and institutions addressing environmental challenges; history of international environmental politics; actors and management of particular global issues.

name: Organizational Psychology
description: Introduction to psychological theories and research applied to behaviour in organizations; topics typically include perception, attitudes, motivation, leadership, teamwork and decision‑making.
